scope: Read-only comparison of new public semiconductor pitches with current Intel LONG screen. Ordinary fund work is not represented as a competition winner. Historical ideas not current recommendations.

examples.name: UConn Student Managed Fund TSM one-pager, 2023 archive
examples.status: Ordinary fund summary, no verified award
examples.limitations: Extremely dense paragraphs and embedded spreadsheet. Mostly technological leadership and end-market demand; does not identify a quantified forecast disagreement. A one-page fund summary is not a direct test of their underlying research depth.
examples.comparison: Our ten-page screen is easier to scan and has a specific margin decomposition, cash funding and downside case. Should not add logo clusters, ESG boilerplate or compressed model screenshots to imitate this.

examples.name: Carleton Sprott Student Investment Fund Micron Hold, 2020
examples.status: Student fund research report, no verified award
examples.useful: PDFpage10 (printed9) supports cyclicality with five years of DRAM/NAND price changes. PDFpage16 (printed15) separates present value from holding-period IRR and shows entry-price versus exit-multiple sensitivities, including negative-return cells. PDFpage18 retains HOLD despite valuation upside because business risk weakens conviction.
examples.limitations: Do not copy its broad semiconductor peer universe as a fully comparable memory-chip group; broad industry shares on p6 do not describe DRAM-specific structure. Several company-description pages are unsuitable for a ten-page screen.
examples.comparison: We already separate planning value and2030 target, but a compact investment-history chart would strengthen the case that40% is durable rather than extrapolating Q3. Need fixed perimeter accounting when comparing old Intel margins. Entry-price sensitivity could make moderate conviction more decision-useful.

examples.name: Notre Dame Investment Club Applied Materials, February2019
examples.status: Ordinary club investment pitch, no verified award
examples.access_note: Web returned text of23-pagePDF initially; later origin404 prevents complete visual inspection. Claims limited to reviewed text.
examples.useful: p8 displays historical price/sales andEV/EBITDA with an explicit why-now discussion; p9 compares R&D spending to competitors and industry wafer-equipment growth. p4-5 explain where the business fits in chip production.
examples.limitations: Historical cheapness is not proof of mispricing, particularly at a cycle peak; R&D spending alone is not return on R&D.
examples.comparison: Current Intel screen describes improving business but does not demonstrate a large initial discount. Better why-now explanation must admit this, not borrow AMAT historical-multiple argument without support.

additional_quality_warning.name: HenryMcKinney / GoldenFlyer Micron2022
additional_quality_warning.status: Author-hosted student pitch, award not verified; first two pages inspected viaweb; origin later502
additional_quality_warning.finding: Page1 states130 target from90.57 entry and calls upside31%; arithmetic is43.54%. Shows why a public pitch is not a vetted gold standard. Do not reproduce its numerical risk probabilities without calibration.

our_strengths: Specific assumptions, funded cash bridge, negative scenarios, explicit uncertainty and readable evidence tables. More disciplined than the reviewed ordinary examples, with unequal lengths/formats acknowledged.
our_main_gaps: p5 demonstrates40% is possible if Q3 profitability persists; it does not independently prove persistence. An across-cycle competitive-margin or cost/mix exhibit is the right next evidentiary improvement.
p6 Oracle billing audit is original but explicitly does not establish chip pricing power or40%margin; avoid letting it stand in as proof of the central long.
p3 uses a single analyst reference with unmatchedEPS conventions, not clean consensus; quantify a comparable same-basis disagreement or label it accurately.
p7 means current price near modeled fair value. A10%return can be an investment case, but cannot be presented as demonstrated mispricing or a high-confidence winning edge.
